_note: M10.4 decision constants. Lives OUTSIDE `m10/screen_registry.json` for the same reason M9's did: the screen registry is pinned by every contrast record and the F verdict, so editing it invalidates them. Same authority — the executor reads THIS file, never prose, never the screen defaults.
_classification_note: NOT an amendment, unlike M9's, which was written after its build. Every field here is fixed BEFORE any M10 six-set number exists and before the build has run. The design it encodes is itself registered upstream in `instructions-m10.md` §Final run and §Goal (amendment A3, 2026-09-04), which is where the four conjuncts and their sequence were fixed.
spec: m10/M102_LOCK.md; design registered in instructions-m10.md §Final run
status: DRAFT until the M10.2 lock commit. `m10src/final10.py` is WRITTEN and unit-tested (19 tests); the SCORING path (loading the six, the bridge) is not.

partitions._headline: clean-4 is M14's registered headline partition for BOTH halves of the pair (Dylan, 2026-09-04), decided before any nano number existed. All six are reported beside it.
partitions._why: stella (the teacher) discloses ArguAna and FiQA in its training data. At a uniform 92% retention fiqa alone supplies ~73% of nano's avg-6 margin, which is why the headline cannot rest on avg-6.

weights: equal within each partition (1/4 on clean-4, 1/6 on all-6), ASSERTED; a partition with a missing dataset must be impossible, not silently renormalized (M9's `_assert_six` lesson)

comparator_source.rule: every conjunct uses ONLY these frozen rows; the freshly-scored bridge anchor is validation-only and discarded
comparator_source._irreplaceable: regenerated from caches that no longer exist. NEVER overwrite it.

sequence.rule: FIXED-SEQUENCE GATEKEEPING in the order C1b -> C1a -> C2a -> C2b, each at the FULL one-sided 0.025, STOPPING AT THE FIRST NON-REJECTION. No Holm, no alpha split: a gatekeeping sequence spends the family alpha once, in a pre-fixed order.
sequence.stop: at the first conjunct that does not reject, every later conjunct is NOT TESTED and is reported as NOT TESTED — never as failed, and never skipped over to reach a later one
sequence._fixed_when: instructions-m10.md §Final run, amendment A3, 2026-09-04 — before any M10 six-set output existed and before the screen ran
sequence._why_this_order: the release conjunct on the headline partition is tested first, so the claim the project is actually making is the one that spends the alpha first. M9's claim-table row 'C1 fail, C2 pass -> aim permitted' is DELETED by this design: an aim conjunct is unreachable if its release conjunct did not reject.

pass_rule: a conjunct rejects only if BOTH the bootstrap bound and the sign-flip test reject at 0.025, inside the sequence. Both, not either.

bootstrap.resample: n_d queries with replacement within each dataset
bootstrap.decision_field_def: np.quantile(draws, 0.025, method='inverted_cdf'), FULL PRECISION — the EMPIRICAL quantile, i.e. the 250th order statistic at B = 10,000
bootstrap._quantile_history: M9 used 0.0125 under Holm-2. M10 uses 0.025 under gatekeeping, which is the whole point of a fixed sequence. The Codex pass of 2026-09-04 found the two quantiles named in different files; 0.025 is operative and is fixed here.
bootstrap.draw_plan: ONE frozen plan per partition, byte-identical across every conjunct that reads that partition, digest serialized
bootstrap._method_note: `inverted_cdf`, never `linear`. NumPy's linear method interpolates toward the next order statistic and returns a weakly HIGHER, more permissive bound, which could flip an irreversible gate in the candidate's favour. This exact defect was caught in M9 by code review before any six-set number existed; it is registered here so it cannot recur.

signflip.signs: independent Rademacher per paired query; every conjunct passes the SAME SEED — a same-seed guarantee, not a materialized shared plan. Sharing is comparability, not a condition of marginal validity.
signflip._alpha_note: `alpha` here and `sequence.alpha_per_conjunct` are the same number by construction: the sign-flip is a conjunct of the same test, at the same level. `decide()` reads the sequence value; this one is documentation and must never diverge.

reserved.trigger: if ANY C-conjunct rejects, then execute, unmodified
reserved._why_any: so an aim claim never stands without its descriptive reserved rows (Opus, §Final run change 1). M9's trigger was `if C1 passes`. **Note, (Codex + Fable adversarial review of the lock, 2026-09-09; both returned DO NOT PUSH): under fixed-sequence gatekeeping 'ANY conjunct rejects' is EQUIVALENT to 'C1b rejects', because C1b is first and nothing later is tested unless it rejected.** The wording is kept as 'any' because it is robust to a future re-ordering, but no reader should think it is a weaker condition than it is.
reserved.leave_one_out: remaining weights renormalized to sum to 1
reserved.fever: labelled a DOUBLE-CONTAMINATED sensitivity row (stella discloses FEVER; it is also a reserved set), zero alpha, never gate-relevant
reserved._one_access: the reserved four carry ONE confirmatory access, unspent through M9.
reserved.crash: per-system atomic outputs; resume at the first incomplete system; scores suppressed until all complete

implementation.reuses: m9src/final_stats.py for the bootstrap and sign-flip primitives; m9src/final9.py's SCORING path
implementation.does_NOT_reuse: `m9src/final9.py:decide()`, which is hard-coded to M9's TWO conjuncts under Holm-2 at 0.0125. An M10 `decide()` for four conjuncts under fixed-sequence gatekeeping at 0.025 is a different function, and reusing the M9 one would silently apply the wrong quantile and the wrong multiplicity correction.
implementation.requirement: written, UNIT-TESTED and REVIEWED before the M10.2 recipe lock is pushed (Codex, 2026-09-04). The tests must include: the sequence stopping at the first non-rejection; a later conjunct reported NOT TESTED rather than failed; the 0.025 quantile being the 250th order statistic and not an interpolated one; and a partition with a missing dataset raising rather than renormalizing.
implementation.status: decide(), the partition-aware bootstrap, the sign-flip wrapper and the registry guard are written and unit-tested (19 tests). REVIEWED 2026-09-09 by Codex and Fable, both of which returned DO NOT PUSH; every finding is applied. STILL OWED: the SCORING path (loading the six, the bridge), which reuses m9src/final9.py's scoring but NEVER its `decide()`, `SPENT_TAG`, `RESULT`, `LEDGER` or `FREEZE` paths — those are M9's.
executor_contract: build EXACTLY ONE draw plan per partition and reuse it byte-identically across both conjuncts that read that partition; serialize its digest. The clean-4 plan is NOT the all-6 plan restricted — it is its own plan over 4 datasets, and the two are not comparable draw-for-draw.
assert the qid arrays are identical across the two conjuncts of a partition before sharing a plan; a shared plan over different qids is not sharing.
compute the bootstrap AND the sign-flip from the SAME `align_partition` output, so both halves of the pass rule see the same validated partition.
score all four conjuncts in ONE transaction regardless of where the sequence stops — the access is spent either way, and the untested conjuncts' descriptive deltas cost nothing.

access_state_machine: m10-six-spent tag PUSHED (before any protected read)
infra_retry_admissible_iff: the m10-six-spent tag does not exist on origin
recover_path: --recover recomputes decisions from results/m10_final_run.json and NEVER re-reads the six
_forbidden_note: in the report's description of any final-run outcome. A screen contrast 'resolves'; a final-run conjunct REJECTS or does not. Keeping the vocabularies apart is what stops a screen verdict being read as a release claim.

headline_verbatim._what: One registered sentence PER OUTCOME, not one string (Codex + Fable adversarial review of the lock, 2026-09-09; both returned DO NOT PUSH): the claim table has two comparators and two partitions, so a single sentence cannot cover it. Each is emitted ONLY if its own conjunct REJECTED, and never if that conjunct was NOT_TESTED.
headline_verbatim.C1b_release_clean4: the selected-teacher-document + nano-query asymmetric system outperformed the bge-small symmetric system on the pre-registered clean-4 partition — NFCorpus, SCIDOCS, SciFact and TREC-COVID — for nDCG@10 in the frozen exact-search harness.
headline_verbatim.C1a_release_avg6: …and on all six development-informed datasets, which additionally include FiQA and ArguAna, both disclosed in the teacher's training data.
headline_verbatim.C2a_aim_avg6: the selected-teacher-document + nano-query asymmetric system outperformed the arctic-document + leaf-query system on the six development-informed datasets in our frozen exact-search harness.
headline_verbatim.C2b_aim_clean4: the selected-teacher-document + nano-query asymmetric system outperformed the arctic-document + leaf-query system on the pre-registered clean-4 partition — NFCorpus, SCIDOCS, SciFact and TREC-COVID — for nDCG@10 in the frozen exact-search harness.
_must_not: any claim about general or untouched retrieval quality
any all-six superiority claim when only a clean-4 conjunct rejected, or the reverse
any aim claim when C2a/C2b were NOT_TESTED
any statement comparing nano's QUERY TOWER to LEAF's — the claim is about the SYSTEM PAIR
retention percentages as the claim; they are a lens, and retention is distribution-specific
the reserved four presented as confirmatory — they are descriptive, at zero alpha
headline_verbatim._stella_disclosure: every sentence carries, in the same paragraph, that the teacher discloses ArguAna and FiQA (2 of the six) in its training data — which is why clean-4 is the headline.

_origin_note: the spend receipt's external witness. Pinned so repointing `origin` cannot manufacture an 'unspent' verdict. Derived from `git remote get-url origin`, never hand-written.
_guard: `final10.assert_evidence_matches_registry` checks quantile, quantile_method, B, k_datasets, the scored dataset set and the sign-flip p-value AT the decision boundary. M9 had `final_stats._assert_matches_registry`; the first draft of M10 removed that protection and replaced it with nothing, and both reviewers demonstrated evidence tagged quantile=0.0125, method='linear', B=9 and even signflip_p=-1 being accepted as REJECTED (Codex + Fable adversarial review of the lock, 2026-09-09; both returned DO NOT PUSH).
forbidden_words_scope: The banned words apply to the REPORT'S CHARACTERISATION OF A FINAL-RUN OUTCOME — never to the screen, whose registered vocabulary is exactly 'resolved' / 'did not resolve' / 'unresolved' (`instructions-m10.md` claim table). Flagged (Codex + Fable adversarial review of the lock, 2026-09-09; both returned DO NOT PUSH) as a contradiction; it is a scoping question, not a conflict: a SCREEN contrast resolves or does not, a FINAL-RUN conjunct rejects or does not, and the report must not swap the two vocabularies.
_ratification: **The one permitted post-commit edit to this file**, and it is not an amendment to any rule: flipping `ratified_by_owner` to true records Dylan's ratification, which the executor requires before the final run may open the six. Registered here explicitly because the review found a deadlock (Codex + Fable adversarial review of the lock, 2026-09-09; both returned DO NOT PUSH) — the lock forbids post-commit edits, the executor refuses to run unless this is true, and a test asserted it must stay false. The test now asserts it is a BOOLEAN and that this clause names the flip as permitted; nothing else about the file may move.
